title: Gas Storage Engineer
setting: Underground Gas Storage (UGS) Operating Facility Technical Office & Transmission Commercial Dispatch Center
agentFocus: Material Balance (p/Z) & Cushion-Working Gas Inventory Reconciliation Agent
headline: The Gas Storage Engineer safeguards the strategic energy balance of the transmission grid, balancing seasonal cyclic inventory, maximizing high-deliverability peak withdrawals, and defending subsurface containment across aging wellbores. While analytical monoliths like Petex MBAL, AspenTech Synergi Gas, and SLB ECLIPSE provide robust thermodynamic and fluid flow engines, they depend entirely on clean, pre-conditioned reservoir data that is fractured across legacy well records, field SCADA historians, and regulatory binders. The gas storage engineer spends 40–60% of technical time manually conditioning noisy shut-in pressure surveys, calculating hysteretic p/Z loops, digitizing multi-vintage wireline cased-hole logs, and assembling manual compliance dossiers for safety audits under API RP 1171 and 49 CFR § 192.12. Rather than attempting to automate subjective reservoir geology, the Gas Storage Engineer requires a federated squad of 7 hyper-specialized agents—each eliminating a concrete friction point in inventory verification, peak deliverability forecasting, wellbore barrier threat evaluation, observation well surveillance, and regulatory filing. Across a seasonal storage cycle, this squad returns ~55.50 hours of high-leverage capacity and integrity engineering time per storage facility, eliminating unrecorded inventory losses, safeguarding against caprock containment breaches, and ensuring peak deliverability during critical grid emergencies.

role.oneLine: Manages underground natural gas storage capacity, inventory reconciliation, cyclic deliverability modeling, and integrity compliance for depleted reservoirs, aquifers, and salt caverns.
role.whyItMatters: Underground gas storage serves as the physical battery and shock absorber for national gas transmission networks and seasonal heating demand. Inaccurate inventory calculations cause multi-million-dollar phantom losses or unrecorded gas migration; deliverability forecast errors cause catastrophic pipeline supply shortfalls during winter peak freezes; and containment breaches or wellbore barrier failures risk catastrophic surface gas releases, public safety disasters, and immediate regulatory shutdown.

variants.name: Depleted Reservoir / Aquifer Storage Engineer
variants.detail: Focuses on porous rock formations; manages large cushion gas volumes, hysteretic p/Z loops, water encroachment (aquifer activity), and multi-well deliverability across large wellfields (50–200 wells).

variants.name: Salt Cavern Storage Engineer
variants.detail: Focuses on solution-mined salt caverns; manages high-deliverability fast-cycling storage, non-isothermal thermodynamics (Joule-Thomson effects), cavern convergence/salt creep, brine handling, and emergency de-brining.

role.titleCheck: The industry title is Gas Storage Engineer or Underground Storage Engineer. Do not confuse with "Pipeline Integrity Engineer" (who oversees linear transmission pipe) or "Classical Reservoir Engineer" (who manages primary production and depletion rather than cyclic seasonal injection/withdrawal).

whereTheWorkHappens.Work Setting: Storage Technical Office & Control Center: Field engineering office situated at the central storage compressor station, with direct network connectivity to transmission control rooms and corporate asset management.
whereTheWorkHappens.What They Can Reach: Multi-monitor workstation running reservoir and hydraulic tools (Petex MBAL, AspenTech Synergi Gas, SLB Petrel/ECLIPSE), plant SCADA historians, wireline cased-hole log viewers, and SIMP compliance databases.
whereTheWorkHappens.Shift Pattern: Standard professional technical hours, with on-call operational support during high-demand winter withdrawal peaks, seasonal turnaround shut-in tests (spring/autumn), and emergency deliverability curtailments.
whereTheWorkHappens.Where the Record Lives: System of record: Corporate Subsurface Database, Storage Well Integrity Management System (SIMP), SCADA data historians, and state/federal regulatory compliance filings (PHMSA/FERC/PNGRB).

vendorGaps.solves: Standard reservoir material balance calculation and surface network delivery optimization.
vendorGaps.gap: Assumes pristine static bottom-hole pressures. Does not autonomously parse seasonal shut-in transients, extract stabilized datum pressures from raw SCADA memory gauges, or track hysteretic p/Z loop deviations for gas migration detection.

vendorGaps.solves: Numerical reservoir simulation of cyclic gas injection and withdrawal, gas-water contact displacement, and aquifer encroachment.
vendorGaps.gap: Heavy setup overhead and static inputs. Simulation models take months to history-match and cannot perform daily operational deliverability forecasting against fluctuating pipeline nominations or ingest real-time wireline log data.

vendorGaps.solves: Surface facility processing simulation, gas dehydration contactors, compressor station operating maps, and transmission network hydraulic dispatch.
vendorGaps.gap: Disconnected from downhole wellbore and reservoir dynamics. Does not link surface network models with well-specific inflow performance (IPR), casing corrosion degradation, or subsurface barrier integrity threat matrices.

actions.action: Calculate seasonal shut-in static bottomhole pressures and construct hysteretic p/Z inventory plots
actions.agentLabel: Agent 1: Material Balance (p/Z) & Cushion-Working Gas Inventory Reconciliation Agent
actions.label: Seasonal Shut-In Pressure Analysis & Hysteretic p/Z Plots (B1, [API-RP-1171 §8])
actions.today: Engineer manually transcribes seasonal shut-in pressure readings from 40–80 wells during spring and autumn turnover, normalizes to formation datum depth, and fits empirical p/Z straight lines or hysteretic loops in Excel.
actions.failureMode: Unstabilized shut-in pressures are mistaken for static equilibrium, disguising unrecorded cushion gas migration into secondary fault compartments or water influx.
actions.agentNote: → Agent 1 (Material Balance (p/Z) & Cushion-Working Gas Inventory Reconciliation Agent).

actions.action: Compute multi-well deliverability drawdown curves and forecast daily peak withdrawal capacity
actions.agentLabel: Agent 2: Peak Withdrawal Deliverability & Dispatch Forecast Agent
actions.label: Multi-Well Deliverability Drawdown & Peak Capacity Forecasting (B1, [API-RP-1171 §6])
actions.today: Commercial pipeline dispatch requests maximum withdrawal nomination for a freezing cold snap; engineer manually aggregates historical backpressure test equations (C and n coefficients) across dozens of wells in spreadsheets.
actions.failureMode: Outdated well deliverability curves fail to account for sandface skin deterioration or gathering line backpressure throttling, causing an unexpected deliverability shortfall during peak grid demand.
actions.agentNote: → Agent 2 (Peak Withdrawal Deliverability & Dispatch Forecast Agent).

actions.action: Correlate multi-finger caliper, cement evaluation, and noise/temperature logs against baseline surveys
actions.agentLabel: Agent 3: Subsurface Integrity & Well Logging Correlation Agent
actions.label: Cased-Hole Well Integrity Log Correlation & Threat Evaluation (B1, [API-RP-1171 §9])
actions.today: Wireline cased-hole inspection logs (multi-finger calipers, acoustic cement bond logs, noise/temperature logs) arrive as PDF and LAS files; engineer spends days comparing current wall-thickness loss against baseline runs.
actions.failureMode: Localized inner or outer casing corrosion defects are overlooked in 50-year-old converted legacy production wells, leading to pinhole leaks into freshwater aquifers or surface casing vent flow.
actions.agentNote: → Agent 3 (Subsurface Integrity & Well Logging Correlation Agent).

actions.action: Monitor peripheral and shallow observation well pressures for containment breaching or migration
actions.agentLabel: Agent 4: Perimeter Observation Well & Containment Anomaly Agent
actions.label: Observation Well Pressure Tracking & Containment Surveillance (B1, [API-RP-1171 §10])
actions.today: Weekly pressure readings from shallow aquifer monitors and peripheral boundary observation wells are gathered from chart recorders and standalone telemetry loggers into spreadsheets.
actions.failureMode: Gradual pressure elevation in an overlying observation zone goes unflagged for months, allowing significant volumes of inventory gas to breach caprock faults before discovery.
actions.agentNote: → Agent 4 (Perimeter Observation Well & Containment Anomaly Agent).

actions.action: Reconcile daily wellhead injection/withdrawal telemetry against pipeline interconnection custody meters
actions.agentLabel: Agent 5: Daily SCADA Meter vs. Storage Balancing Agent
actions.label: Daily SCADA Meter vs. Custody Transfer Interconnection Balancing (B1, [API-RP-1171 §11])
actions.today: Storage engineer cross-references daily SCADA wellhead orifice meter logs, compressor fuel usage receipts, and dehydrator vent estimates against pipeline custody transfer billing meters in Excel.
actions.failureMode: Cumulative meter calibration drift or gathering line packing variations mask an unrecorded pipeline gathering line pinhole leak, resulting in unresolved physical inventory variances.
actions.agentNote: → Agent 5 (Daily SCADA Meter vs. Storage Balancing Agent).

actions.action: Track thermodynamic pressure-temperature cycles and volumetric convergence in salt storage caverns
actions.agentLabel: Agent 6: Salt Cavern Thermodynamic & Creep Surveillance Agent
actions.label: Salt Cavern Thermodynamic Cycle & Creep Convergence Tracking (B1, [API-RP-1170 §7])
actions.today: High-deliverability salt cavern undergoes aggressive multi-cycle withdrawal; engineer calculates Joule-Thomson cooling effects and hand-checks sonar volumetric point-cloud surveys to evaluate cavern closure rates.
actions.failureMode: Rapid withdrawal chilling drops cavern gas temperature below structural design criteria, inducing thermal cracking in the salt ceiling or casing shoe shear failure.
actions.agentNote: → Agent 6 (Salt Cavern Thermodynamic & Creep Surveillance Agent).

actions.action: Compile Storage Integrity Management Program (SIMP) compliance dossiers and risk assessment records
actions.agentLabel: Agent 7: Regulatory Storage Safety (SIMP) & Compliance Audit Dossier Agent
actions.label: Storage Integrity Management Program (SIMP) Regulatory Filing (B1, [PHMSA-192 §192.12])
actions.today: The engineering team spends 3 to 4 weeks each year compiling well barrier risk scores, mechanical integrity test certificates, and observation pressure logs into audit dossiers for pipeline safety regulators.
actions.failureMode: Missing inspection documentation or inconsistent threat assessments result in formal regulatory warning letters, mandatory operating pressure derating, or severe civil penalties.
actions.agentNote: → Agent 7 (Regulatory Storage Safety (SIMP) & Compliance Audit Dossier Agent).

actions.action: History-match 3D compositional or black-oil reservoir simulation models of cyclic gas storage fields
actions.label: 3D Numerical Reservoir Simulation History-Matching (B2, [EN-1918-1 §6])
actions.today: Executed in SLB ECLIPSE or Petex MBAL. The engineer sets geological fault transmissibilities, relative permeability hysteresis curves, and aquifer water influx models.
actions.agentNote: ❌ No. Core subsurface interpretation craft. The numerical simulator computes multi-phase grid physics; the engineer provides geological and geomechanical context.

actions.action: Model complex surface compressor station piping acoustics and dehydration contactor hydraulics
actions.label: Surface Compressor Station & Facility Hydraulics Modeling (B2, [GPSA Data Book §13])
actions.today: Handled in Aspen HYSYS or Synergi Gas. Solves gas dehydration kinetics, compressor station horsepower curves, and surface gathering line pressure drops.
actions.agentNote: ❌ No. Solved by established process and pipeline hydraulic monoliths.

actions.action: Authorize maximum allowable operating pressure (MAOP) re-certifications and safety margin adjustments
actions.label: Maximum Allowable Operating Pressure (MAOP) Certification (B3, [PHMSA-192 §192.12])
actions.today: Formal technical and legal sign-off establishing reservoir and wellhead operating pressure limits based on caprock fracture gradient and casing burst ratings.
actions.agentNote: ❌ No. Statutory and professional engineering accountability cannot be delegated to an automated agent.

actions.action: Execute wireline mechanical barrier pressure testing and surface safety valve (SSSV) inflow tests
actions.label: Well Mechanical Barrier Inflow & Pressure Testing (B3, [ISO-16530-1 §8])
actions.today: Field technicians and wireline crews deploy slickline plugs, close subsurface safety valves (SSSV), and monitor annular pressure bleed-off tests.
actions.agentNote: ❌ No. Hands-on physical operation conducted at the wellhead in hazardous field zones.

actions.action: Design and supervise hydraulic fracturing, reperforation, or gravel pack cleanout well workovers
actions.label: Workover Intervention Design & Remedial Cementing (B2, [API-RP-1171 §9])
actions.today: Well engineering software (Landmark COMPASS / WellCAT) is used to design casing patch liners, squeeze cementing programs, and sand control completions.
actions.agentNote: ❌ No. Solved by drilling and completions monoliths with specialized wellbore mechanics modules.

actions.action: Screen gas storage wells for near-wellbore water coning and liquid loading during high-rate withdrawal
actions.label: Liquid Loading & Water Coning Screening (B1, [API-RP-1171 §6])
actions.today: Engineer evaluates critical Turner velocity and water-gas ratios on high-rate withdrawal wells; flags wells requiring chemical soap sticks, velocity strings, or deliquification work.
actions.failureMode: Unnoticed liquid loading chokes well deliverability mid-winter or causes severe water slugging into surface separation equipment.
actions.agentNote: Covered in Agent 2 (Peak Withdrawal Deliverability & Dispatch Forecast Agent).

actions.action: Evaluate caprock threshold capillary displacement pressure and geomechanical fault seal integrity
actions.label: Caprock Geomechanical Seal & Threshold Pressure Evaluation (B2, [EN-1918-2 §5])
actions.today: Core laboratory step-rate mercury injection testing and geomechanical finite-element stress modeling are performed to evaluate fault reactivation risks.
actions.agentNote: ❌ No. High-touch specialized laboratory geomechanics and specialized subsurface rock mechanics analysis.

actions.action: Testify at federal and state utility regulatory rate cases regarding storage capacity and cushion gas
actions.label: Utility Regulatory Rate Case & Capacity Certification Testimony (B3, Corporate Policy)
actions.today: Senior storage engineers prepare and deliver formal sworn testimony before utility commissions regarding working gas capacity, cushion gas valuation, and tariff deliverability guarantees.
actions.agentNote: ❌ No. Strategic corporate executive representation and legal proceeding governance.

agents.name: Material Balance (p/Z) & Cushion-Working Gas Inventory Reconciliation Agent
agents.oneLine: Ingests seasonal shut-in pressure surveys, normalizes datum pressures, computes gas compressibility z-factors, and constructs hysteretic p/Z inventory plots to detect unrecorded gas migration or water encroachment.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates ~4.75 hours per seasonal survey of manual gauge de-noising, Horner shut-in pressure extrapolation, and hysteretic spreadsheet plotting.
agents.reads: Individual well shut-in surface and bottomhole pressure memory gauge surveys, gas chromatographic gas composition reports, and cumulative injected/withdrawn inventory records.
agents.does: Filters gauge pressure drift; extrapolates semi-steady-state datum static pressure using Horner / Superposition methods; calculates non-linear real gas z-factors (Hall-Yarborough / Dranchuk-Abu-Kassem correlations); constructs seasonal p/Z versus cumulative gas inventory curves; highlights slope divergences between injection and withdrawal legs indicating water drive or thief-zone gas loss.
agents.returns: Seasonal p/Z Inventory Balance Dossier with calculated effective pore volume, base cushion gas verification, and anomalous gas migration flags.
agents.stopsAt: Re-classifying booked cushion gas to working gas on corporate financial ledgers.
agents.failureModes: If well shut-in duration is too brief to achieve radial stabilization (dP/dt > 0.05 psi/hr), the agent tags: [Unstabilized Shut-In: Datum Pressure Estimate Carries High Uncertainty Envelope].

agents.name: Peak Withdrawal Deliverability & Dispatch Forecast Agent
agents.oneLine: Couples multi-well inflow performance relationships (IPR) with gathering system backpressure curves to predict maximum 24-hour field withdrawal capacity across varying inventory levels and screen for liquid loading.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates ~4.50 hours per commercial dispatch nomination cycle of recalculating individual well deliverability tables, choke settings, and critical unloading velocities.
agents.reads: Current reservoir static datum pressure, historical well backpressure test coefficients (C and n), tubing hydraulic tables (VLP), gathering manifold pressures, and gas-water ratio trends.
agents.does: Calculates sandface pressure drawdown per well; solves inflow-outflow nodal intersections; evaluates critical gas velocity against Turner and Coleman droplet models to detect liquid loading risks; sums deliverability across available wells under compressor suction constraints; forecasts maximum sustainable 24-hour withdrawal rate.
agents.returns: Dispatch Deliverability Forecast Matrix ranking available wells by deliverability efficiency, accompanied by liquid loading vulnerability alerts.
agents.stopsAt: Opening or closing physical wellhead choke valves or throttling compressor station suction control loops.
agents.failureModes: If requested commercial dispatch rate exceeds formation sand-production drawdown thresholds, the agent flags: [Deliverability Warning: Sandface Critical Drawdown Exceeded — Severe Sand Influx Risk].

agents.name: Subsurface Integrity & Well Logging Correlation Agent
agents.oneLine: Cross-correlates multi-finger casing caliper, acoustic cement bond (CBL/VDL), and noise/temperature logs against baseline surveys to quantify casing metal loss and evaluate wellbore barrier integrity under API RP 1171.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates ~6.00 hours per cased-hole logging evaluation of manual curve depth-matching, baseline trace subtraction, and corrosion defect severity calculations.
agents.reads: Multi-finger caliper log files (raw 24/40/60 arm radius curves), ultrasonic casing inspection logs, cement evaluation logs (CBL/VDL), noise/temperature logs, and historical well completion diagrams.
agents.does: Slices and depth-aligns raw caliper logs against original baseline surveys; computes remaining burst and collapse resistance based on maximum pit depth and general corrosion metal loss; identifies channeling in annular cement sheaths; flags fluid movement behind casing from noise/temperature anomalies; maps integrity data into API RP 1171 well threat matrices.
agents.returns: Well Integrity Cased-Hole Evaluation Report with ranked casing defect locations, calculated remaining burst safety factors, and workover priority scores.
agents.stopsAt: Issuing mandatory well shut-in or plugging orders.
agents.failureModes: If metal loss exceeds 50% of nominal wall thickness within the gas storage interval, the agent triggers: [Severe Barrier Defect: Primary Well Barrier Penetration Exceeds API RP 1171 Safety Margin].

agents.name: Perimeter Observation Well & Containment Anomaly Agent
agents.oneLine: Screens continuous pressure and fluid level telemetry from peripheral, caprock, and overlying formation observation wells to identify gas migration, caprock fault activation, or spill-point breaching.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates ~4.00 hours per weekly surveillance cycle of manual telemetry data collation, baseline hydrostatic subtraction, and observation well pressure trending.
agents.reads: Daily telemetry pressure and liquid level feeds from shallow groundwater monitors, overlying porous formation observation wells, peripheral spill-point wells, and annular surface casing pressures.
agents.does: Filters barometric and tidal pressure oscillations; subtracts expected hydrostatic groundwater baselines; tracks rate of pressure change (dP/dt) in non-storage formations; computes pressure differential between storage reservoir and overlying observation zones; identifies anomalous gas-water contact shifts approaching geological spill points.
agents.returns: Weekly Containment Surveillance Dashboard highlighting observation wells with statistically significant pressure anomalies, with spatial migration vector overlays.
agents.stopsAt: Redefining geological spill points or altering reservoir operating boundaries.
agents.failureModes: If pressure in an overlying shallow observation zone increases by >10 psi within 7 days, the agent triggers an immediate alert: [Containment Alert: Overlying Horizon Pressure Anomaly — Possible Caprock Breach or Tubing-Casing Leak].

agents.name: Daily SCADA Meter vs. Storage Balancing Agent
agents.oneLine: Reconciles daily high-frequency SCADA wellhead flowmeter telemetry, compressor fuel combustion logs, and dehydrator vent estimates against pipeline custody transfer interconnection meters.
agents.frictionSolved: Removes ~3.50 hours per daily/weekly allocation cycle of cross-referencing multi-meter spreadsheets, investigating meter calibration drift, and tracking line pack.
agents.reads: High-frequency SCADA wellhead orifice/ultrasonic flowmeters, compressor fuel consumption records, dehydration separator liquid dump counters, flare/vent flow records, and pipeline custody transfer fiscal meter tickets.
agents.does: Calculates theoretical field injection/withdrawal mass totals; accounts for surface line pack adjustments using AGA-8 thermodynamic gas densities; compares field aggregate against custody interconnect meters; highlights individual meter runs drifting outside standard calibration tolerances (±1.5%).
agents.returns: Daily Storage Volume Reconciliation Balance Sheet isolating meter imbalance hot spots and surfacing unmetered fuel/vent volume discrepancies.
agents.stopsAt: Overriding official custody transfer billing invoices or certified pipeline exchange statements.
agents.failureModes: If unexplained physical volume imbalance between wellhead aggregate and custody delivery exceeds 2.0% for 48 consecutive hours, the agent flags: [Unresolved Material Balance Gap: Surface Facility Piping Leak or Major Meter Calibration Failure Suspected].

agents.name: Salt Cavern Thermodynamic & Creep Surveillance Agent
agents.oneLine: Models transient non-isothermal gas expansion thermodynamics and processes sonar point-cloud surveys to monitor salt cavern convergence, prevent wall tensile failure, and safeguard cavern operating envelopes.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates ~4.75 hours per cavern cycling analysis of manual thermodynamic gas expansion math, temperature profile reconstruction, and sonar survey volume comparisons.
agents.reads: High-frequency cavern wellhead and downhole pressure/temperature sensors, gas injection/withdrawal mass flow rates, historical sonar cavern geometry point clouds, and regional salt creep geomechanical parameters.
agents.does: Solves non-isothermal dynamic energy balance equations (Joule-Thomson thermal drops during rapid high-rate withdrawal); predicts gas temperature drops at the cavern wall and casing shoe; compares successive sonar point-cloud geometries to calculate volumetric creep convergence; validates cavern operating conditions against API RP 1170 minimum/maximum pressure envelopes.
agents.returns: Cavern Thermodynamic & Structural Envelope Dossier with projected casing shoe temperatures, volumetric loss rates, and allowable cycle withdrawal rate caps.
agents.stopsAt: Ordering emergency brine injection or shut-in of cavern withdrawal operations.
agents.failureModes: If simulated gas temperature at the cavern roof drops below +32^circF during high-rate withdrawal, the agent raises a critical alert: [Thermal Integrity Threat: Cavern Roof Chilled Near Freezing Point — Salt Micro-Fracturing Risk].

agents.name: Regulatory Storage Safety (SIMP) & Compliance Audit Dossier Agent
agents.oneLine: Aggregates well barrier risk scores, mechanical integrity test certificates, observation well pressure logs, and preventive maintenance records into audit-ready compliance dossiers for PHMSA 49 CFR § 192.12 and API RP 1171 audits.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates ~28.00 hours per annual audit cycle of cross-referencing paper records, transcribing well test certificates, and compiling regulatory filings.
agents.reads: Subsurface Well Integrity Management Program (SIMP) risk assessment matrices, annual mechanical integrity test (MIT) pressure logs, casing caliper inspection records, surface safety valve test tickets, and observation well pressure histories.
agents.does: Bins well inventory into regulatory risk tiers; maps preventive maintenance and logging history against mandatory re-inspection intervals; compiles multi-well barrier status scorecards; formats required annual reporting forms (e.g., PHMSA Form F7100.4-1 / state regulatory equivalents); generates traceability links connecting every risk score to supporting raw gauge/log files.
agents.returns: Audit-Ready Annual SIMP Compliance Dossier with executive summary, well risk tier rankings, and mandatory inspection compliance tracking tables.
agents.stopsAt: Legally certifying or electronically signing official government compliance filings.
agents.failureModes: If an active gas storage well has exceeded its mandatory 5-year or 10-year mechanical integrity re-inspection interval without an approved deferral, the agent flags: [Regulatory Non-Compliance Alert: Well Exceeded Mandated MIT Inspection Interval — Operating Violation].

negativeSearch.result: Negative Search, 2026-09. Incumbent simulation and network hydraulic software packages solve thermodynamic and pressure equations assuming clean, manually assembled boundary conditions; none autonomously correlate multi-vintage cased-hole integrity logs against storage risk matrices, de-noise high-frequency observation well pressure drifts, or reconcile pipeline commercial dispatch deliverability against real-time wellbore liquid loading without extensive manual engineer data formatting.

line: "In underground gas storage, spending days wrestling with disjointed spreadsheets to calculate p/Z points and transcribing wireline caliper logs into risk binders is not integrity management; it is clerical friction that leaves the storage engineer blind to subtle observation well pressure drifts until gas is already migrating through a breached caprock."
openQuestions: How many days does your engineering team spend during the spring and autumn turnover seasons manually compiling pressure-volume-temperature data to construct the annual p/Z hysteretic inventory curve?

When pipeline dispatch demands maximum emergency deliverability during a winter polar vortex, how quickly can you verify which wells risk hydrate freezing, water coning, or sandface failure under aggressive drawdown?

How do you currently correlate historical multi-finger casing caliper logs and cement evaluation runs across dozens of 50-year-old converted production wells to satisfy API RP 1171 and 49 CFR § 192.12 integrity mandates?
